comments.text:
When I was girl, my Dad supported our family by being a Union Retail Grocery Clerk. We had a nice home, good clothes, medical and dental. We had two cars, my mother didn't work. Employees had guaranteed hours and raises, and access to training programs for even further advancement.  And that was pretty standard.
We had a travel vacation every summer, went to Disneyland in 1967, went to Yellowstone Park, Grand Coulee Dam, sometimes camped at the ocean. My Sis went to college all paid for, had an apt and car paid for the whole time and got her degree. 
Supported that family lifestyle on ONE CAREER as an AFL-CIO Retail Clerk.
But the public broke the union...
Now...clerks are sitting ducks, every creep with an ankle monitor knows there's a waiting target at the convenience store.
Shoppers get the experience they pay for. They didn't want to shop at union stores, and pay 3 cents more on items, so their working neighbors could have dental and medical.
Shoppers wanted cheap...and shoppers are getting cheap...in every way.
